skill.name: ensembl-database
skill.description: Query the Ensembl REST API for gene lookups, sequence retrieval, variant effects, comparative genomics, and assembly mapping across many species.
skill.summary: Query Ensembl REST data for genes, variants, sequences, assemblies, and orthologs.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The confirmed findings are expected outbound Ensembl REST requests from the helper script and documentation examples. I found no prompt injection, malware intent, credential access, local system reconnaissance, or automatic shell execution.

remediation.issue: Outbound Ensembl requests disclose user query terms.
remediation.suggestion: Document that gene symbols, variants, regions, and species names are sent to Ensembl REST servers.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes optional package installation commands.
remediation.suggestion: State that package installation requires user approval and prefer pinned versions in examples.

remediation.issue: Path values are interpolated into REST endpoint strings.
remediation.suggestion: URL-encode or validate species, gene, variant, and region path segments before requests.

content.value_statement: Genomics work often needs precise Ensembl identifiers, sequences, variants, and assembly context. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Ensembl REST queries and reports.
actual_capabilities: Look up genes by symbol, Ensembl ID, or external database identifier.
Retrieve genomic, transcript, coding, and protein sequences from Ensembl endpoints.
Query variants and run VEP-style consequence lookups by HGVS notation.
Find orthologs, paralogs, gene trees, and comparative genomics records.
Map coordinates between genome assemblies, including GRCh37 and current assemblies.
Use a Python helper script with rate limiting and basic retry handling.
limitations: Requires internet access to Ensembl REST servers.
Results depend on the current Ensembl release and endpoint availability.
Does not replace validated clinical variant interpretation.
Large batch workflows need caching and careful rate-limit handling.

use_cases.title: Annotate a Gene List
use_cases.description: Convert gene symbols into Ensembl IDs, coordinates, transcript summaries, and external references.

use_cases.title: Review Variant Consequences
use_cases.description: Query known variants or HGVS strings and summarize predicted consequences and population context.

use_cases.title: Compare Orthologs Across Species
use_cases.description: Find related genes across organisms and collect sequence or homology context for comparison.

prompt_templates.title: Look Up One Gene
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Ensembl database skill to look up [gene symbol] in [species]. Summarize the Ensembl ID, location, transcripts, and useful cross-references.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieve a Sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve the [genomic, cDNA, CDS, or protein] sequence for [Ensembl ID]. Return the sequence source, assembly context, and any important parameters.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Variant
prompt_templates.prompt: Query Ensembl for [variant ID or HGVS notation] in [species]. Summarize predicted consequences, affected genes, transcript impacts, and population data when available.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Comparative Report
prompt_templates.prompt: For [gene or Ensembl ID], find orthologs in [target species], retrieve relevant sequences, and compare coordinates, transcripts, and conservation notes.

output_examples.input: Find BRCA2 information for human and summarize transcripts.
output_examples.output: A concise gene summary with the Ensembl ID, chromosome location, transcript overview, external references, and query parameters used.

output_examples.input: Check rs699 in human and explain likely consequences.
output_examples.output: A variant report with known alleles, mapped genes, predicted functional effects, population frequency context, and source endpoint notes.

output_examples.input: Compare a human gene with mouse orthologs.
output_examples.output: A comparative summary with ortholog identifiers, species names, homology type, sequence retrieval options, and follow-up analysis suggestions.

best_practices: Confirm the species name, assembly, and identifier type before querying.
Use batch endpoints and caching for repeated or large-scale requests.
Record Ensembl release, endpoint, and parameters with every result.
anti_patterns: Do not treat Ensembl annotations as clinical conclusions without expert review.
Do not send sensitive sample metadata unless disclosure to Ensembl is acceptable.
Do not ignore rate limits when running many requests.

faq.question: Does this skill need internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. It queries Ensembl REST servers and related documentation over HTTPS.

faq.question: Can it work with human and non-human species?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports Ensembl species identifiers such as human, mouse, zebrafish, and many others.

faq.question: Can it retrieve FASTA sequences?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper script and examples include sequence retrieval in JSON or FASTA formats.

faq.question: Does it support older genome assemblies?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance includes GRCh37 and current Ensembl REST server selection.

faq.question: Can it interpret clinical significance?
faq.answer: No. It can gather annotations and variant consequences, but clinical interpretation needs validated expert review.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
